Two-Stage Sorting is a sorting optimization for volume rendering pipelines that splits the generation of depth-sorted per-tile splat lists into two separate radix sort routines to reduce VRAM usage and computational complexity [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Two-Stage Sorting is a sorting optimization for volume rendering pipelines that splits the generation of depth-sorted per-tile splat lists into two separate radix sort routines to reduce VRAM usage and computational complexity. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in Section B.2: it describes separating the sorting step into two routines (one for depth ordering, one for per-tile lists), notes that this allows using smaller keys (32-bit and 16-bit) thereby reducing VRAM usage, and provides a complexity analysis showing a reduction from O(384n) to O(160n) (O(32n) + O(128n)). The source also specifies that a stable sorting algorithm like radix sort is required.
